faq.a: JavaScript regular expressions — the same syntax used in browsers and Node.js. Most patterns transfer to other languages, but lookbehind, named groups, and flag support differ by flavor.
Every match is listed in order with its index in the text and any capture groups it contains. Matching is always global here so you can see all results at once.

whenNotToUse: A pattern that works here may still behave differently in Python, Java, or PCRE — check flavor-specific features (like \K or possessive quantifiers) before porting.
Catastrophic patterns (nested quantifiers on long input) can hang any regex engine — if the page stalls, shorten the test text and simplify the pattern.
